params.body:
A post on TikTok, Instagram or YouTube can now be cited by its link.

Adding a source by its link fetches the page and reads its title and text. These three platforms show a login wall or an empty page built by scripts to anything that is not a browser, so the fetch read nothing and the link was refused ("The page gave no text to read"). With the source checks (#446), a link that cannot be cited holds a post back, and posts about youth culture link to these platforms all the time.

## What changes (`citeLink` in `packages/core/source-by-link.mjs`)

- `platformOf(link)` recognises tiktok.com, instagram.com, youtube.com and youtu.be, including their subdomains (`vm.tiktok.com`, `m.youtube.com`).
- A link on one of them that the Observatory does not hold yet is not fetched. It is held as a signal under "Cited by the author", with the platform, the publisher (TikTok, Instagram, YouTube), and the text `TikTok post`, and it is cited under its sentence as before.
- **The writer's sentence never becomes the signal's text.** It is kept in the meta as `citedFor`, with `unread: true`. Otherwise the Observatory would classify a claim of ours as something it observed.
- Unchanged: a held post is cited as it is, and the same post is held once. Links on a source read for inspiration only are still refused. The platforms are not queued as publishers (`NOT_A_PUBLISHER` already skips them).

## Tests

- `test/source-by-link.test.mjs` (13): the platforms and their short and mobile hosts, not a path that merely mentions one; a TikTok link cited without a fetch, with platform, text and `citedFor`, and once only.
- Full suite 1650/1650, `tsc` clean.
params.title: Cite TikTok, Instagram and YouTube posts without a fetch
